title: Meet Carignan
subtitle: High acid, high tannin, old vines

steps.title: A rustic grape
steps.body: Carignan gives deep-coloured wines with red and black fruit, dried herbs, liquorice and earthy, sometimes meaty notes. It has high acidity, high tannin and can be rustic and astringent when young or overcropped. From old, low-yielding vines, it becomes concentrated and complex.
steps.highlight: Dark fruit, herbs, high acid and tannin

steps.title: Spanish roots
steps.body: Carignan comes from Aragón, in Spain, near the town of Cariñena. In Spain it's also called Mazuelo, in Rioja, and Samsó, in Catalonia. In Italy, mainly Sardinia, it's Carignano. It buds late and ripens very late, so it needs heat. It's vigorous and can yield heavily, which is why it became a bulk grape.

steps.prompt: Match each name to where it's used.
steps.explanation: Carignan takes a new name in each region.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Carignan often appears in blends, adding colour, acidity and structure. On its own, look for deep colour, bright acidity, firm tannin and earthy, herbal notes. Old-vine examples are richer, with dark fruit and spice. Its high acidity sets it apart from Grenache, its usual partner.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Carignan has high acidity, high tannin and earthy notes
It comes from Cariñena in Aragón and has many names
It ripens late and needs heat
